examples.solution_text:
Angles forming a right angle add to $90^{\circ}$.

$\begin{align*}34^{\circ}+x&=90^{\circ}\\x&=90^{\circ}-34^{\circ}\\x&=56^{\circ}\end{align*}$

The two angles are complementary, so they add to $90^{\circ}$.

$\begin{align*}52^{\circ}+b&=90^{\circ}\\b&=90^{\circ}-52^{\circ}\\b&=38^{\circ}\end{align*}$

examples.derivation: The outside arms lie at 0° and 90°. The internal ray lies at 34°, so x = 90° − 34° = 56°. This follows the complementary-angle subtraction taught in Trigonometry B lines 119–130 and its supplied image14.png.

The outside arms lie at 20° and 110°, forming 90°. The internal ray at 72° gives a known angle of 72° − 20° = 52° and b = 110° − 72° = 38°. Independently, 90° − 52° = 38°. The rotated square correctly marks the outside right angle.
